history.summary: THIS IS THE SMALL VITTHAL-RAKHUMAI TEMPLE IN ALANDI TOWN ON THE INDRAYANI RIVERBANK — NOT the famous 12th/13th-century Shri Vitthal-Rukmini Mandir at Pandharpur (Solapur district), one of the 108 Abhimana Kshetrams; do not conflate the two. The Alandi shrine, one of the town's cluster of temples (with Ram, Krishna, and Muktai temples), is dedicated to Lord Vitthal (Vithoba), a form of Vishnu/Krishna, and his consort Rukmini (locally Rakhumai). Standalone history, founding date, and architecture of the Alandi shrine are UNVERIFIED in web sources; the documented Pandharpur history (Hoysala king Vishnuvardhana 1108–1152 CE, 1237 CE Vira Someshwara inscription, 17th-century Deccan-style rebuild) applies to Pandharpur, not Alandi. Coordinates are APPROXIMATE (Alandi town centre; exact shrine location unverified).

name: Vitthal-Rukmini Temple
town_description: Alandi is a pilgrimage town in Khed taluka of Pune district, Maharashtra, on the banks of the Indrayani River about 19–22 km northeast of Pune. It is best known as the place where Sant Dnyaneshwar took sanjeevan samadhi in 1296. Besides the samadhi mandir, the town has the Vitthal-Rakhumai, Ram, Krishna, and Muktai temples, and is the starting point of the annual Dnyaneshwar Palkhi procession to Pandharpur.

travel.road: ~22 km northeast of Pune; buses from Swargate Bus Station, Pune; taxis/private cabs available
